quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian paprika isn't just a spice—it's a national treasure! Hungary has eight different types of paprika, ranging from delicate and sweet to fiery hot. The town of Szeged is so famous for its paprika that it hosts an annual paprika festival every October.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals, like those you might spot in the Strait of Juan de Fuca, can hold their breath for up to 30 minutes and dive nearly 1,500 feet deep. Learn about the fascinating behaviors of these charming marine mammals.

medium_read.title: Budapest's Thermal Baths: A Living Tradition
medium_read.teaser: For over 2,000 years, Hungarians have been soaking in therapeutic thermal waters, a tradition that continues today in Budapest's magnificent bathhouses. Discover the history and culture behind this beloved Hungarian ritual.

long_read.title: Olympic National Park: Where Wilderness Meets Wonder
long_read.teaser: From temperate rainforests to alpine peaks to wild Pacific coastline, Olympic National Park contains an incredible diversity of ecosystems right in your backyard. This gorgeous exploration reveals why it's one of America's greatest natural treasures.

port_angeles.title: Butterfly Garden at the Clallam County Courthouse
port_angeles.description: The beautiful butterfly garden at the Clallam County Courthouse attracts dozens of butterfly species throughout late summer and early fall. September is a wonderful time to visit and watch monarchs, swallowtails, and painted ladies fluttering among the native flowers. It's a peaceful spot right in downtown Port Angeles.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You know your hummingbird facts! Their tiny hearts work incredibly hard to power those fast-beating wings.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute—that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are truly amazing—they beat about 1,200 times per minute! That's what it takes to power those remarkable hovering abilities.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Rufous hummingbirds pass through the Olympic Peninsula during migration and are known for their incredible journeys—some travel over 3,000 miles from Alaska to Mexico!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'hello' or 'goodbye'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Szia! That's right! It's such a friendly, versatile word—perfect for both hellos and goodbyes.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Szia' (pronounced 'SEE-ah')—it's the informal way Hungarians say both hello and goodbye to friends and family!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language—it's part of the Finno-Ugric family, making it completely different from neighboring European languages. It's known for its beautiful sounds and complex grammar.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree is the oldest living thing in Olympic National Park?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Western Red Cedars can live over 1,000 years in the Olympic Peninsula. These magnificent giants were sacred to Native peoples and provided materials for canoes, houses, and clothing.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the Western Red Cedar! Some in the park are over 1,000 years old. These majestic trees have witnessed centuries of history on the Olympic Peninsula.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Quinault Rain Forest in Olympic National Park is home to some of the largest Western Red Cedars in the world. Indigenous peoples called them 'Long Life Maker' for their many uses.
